body.statement: For a finite directed graph with \(n_D\) vertices and \(m_D\) edges, a root \(r\), and terminals \(W_D\) not containing \(r\), all inclusion-minimal subgraphs containing a directed \(r\)-to-\(w\) path for every \(w\in W_D\) can be enumerated with \(O(n_D+m_D)\) worst-case delay after \(O(n_Dm_D)\) preprocessing and with \(O(n_D^2)\) working space.

source.locator: Theorem 16 in Section 5.2, arXiv:2010.11462v4; PODS 2022, pages 301--313
source.verbatim_statement: Directed Steiner Tree Enumeration can be solved in amortized \(O(n+m)\) time and \(O(n+m)\) space. If we allow \(O(nm)\) preprocessing time, this problem can be solved in \(O(n+m)\) delay with \(O(n^2)\) space.

attestation.note: Literal primary-source transcription from arXiv:2010.11462v4 HTML, Theorem 16, accessed 2026-09-13.

body.justification: This supplies the raw minimal directed-Steiner enumerator used after deterministic-reachability projection.
body.gap: The published theorem does not treat fixed deterministic edges, uncertain-edge support projection, or global domination across causal cores; those adaptations are proved in Theorem~\ref{thm:canonical-enumeration}.
body.consumer: It provides polynomial work between raw projected witnesses, while the causal theorem performs support canonicalization and global filtering.
